claim: NVIDIA's Jetson lifecycle page lists Jetson AGX Orin 64GB/32GB, Orin NX 16GB/8GB and Orin Nano 8GB/4GB as 'Available through' January 2032; AGX Orin Industrial through July 2033.
NVIDIA's Jetson lifecycle page lists Jetson T5000 available through August 2035 and Jetson T4000 through January 2036.
The Jetson lifecycle page covers hardware availability only; it states no software-support duration and promises an EOL notice at least 8 months before last shipment.
Jetson Linux r32 releases span 32.1 (March 2019) to 32.7.6 (November 2024), about 5 years 8 months of updates for one branch.
Jetson Linux r34/r35 releases span 34.1 (April 2022) to 35.7.0 (October 2026); the branch was still receiving releases 4.5 years after first release.
Jetson Linux r36 (Orin) releases span 36.2 (December 2023) to 36.5.2 (August 2026); r39.2 (June 2026) and 39.2.1 (August 2026) support T5000, T4000, AGX Orin, Orin NX and Orin Nano.
JetPack 7 is 'Built on Linux Kernel 6.8 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS' and supports Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor; JetPack 7.2 officially supports Yocto via OE4T and includes a preemptable real-time kernel.

JetPack 7.2 / Jetson Linux 39.2 (dated 6/02/2026) 'Adds support for the Jetson Orin product family within JetPack 7 releases' and 'Provides official Yocto recipes for Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms through the OE4T GitHub repository'; it lists 'Canonical Ubuntu 24.04 for Jetson' as another supported distro.

Jetson Linux 39.2.1 Real-Time Kernel 'support is provided with Developer-Preview quality' for Jetson T5000, AGX Orin, Orin NX and Orin Nano, installed as Debian packages (nvidia-l4t-rt-kernel etc.) from repo.download.nvidia.com/jetson/rt-kernel.
Isaac ROS says its PREEMPT_RT kernel for JetPack 7.2 'is recommended only for use with robot manipulators'.

NVIDIA's Bring Your Own Kernel page lists upstreamed Tegra patches from v5.15 to v6.7, says out-of-tree modules are provided for drivers that 'cannot be upstreamed or that have not yet been upstreamed', and calls the NVIDIA kernel source 'the most complete and best tested'.
Mainline Linux v6.18 contains device trees for Orin (tegra234-p3701, p3737, p3767, p3768) and Thor (tegra264-p3834, p3971) in arch/arm64/boot/dts/nvidia.

Jetson Linux bootloader redundancy is enabled by default; a slot that fails to boot is marked unbootable and roles switch; bootloader is updated by UEFI capsule to the non-current slot; nvbootctrl 'is intended to be used for debugging'.

OE4T docs: 'By default, both the stock NVIDIA provided Jetpack image as well as OE4T images use the non redundant partition layouts'; choosing a redundant layout at the outset 'might give you the option to support updates later without a repartition (or tegraflash)'.

meta-tegra (MIT) maintained branches as of its 01 Oct 2026 page: master/blacksail/wrynose (LTS) track L4T R39.2.1/JetPack 7.2.1 for AGX Orin/Orin NX/Orin Nano/AGX Thor; scarthgap (LTS) tracks R36.5.2/JetPack 6.2.3 and 'will stay on R36.x/JetPack 6.x'.
meta-tegra contributor concentration: top contributor madisongh 2,373 commits vs next 189 (GitHub contributor stats, 2026-11-10).
The OE4T tegra-demo-distro ships an SWUpdate demo image that 'supports A/B rootfs updates' and requires USE_REDUNDANT_FLASH_LAYOUT=1.

mendersoftware/meta-mender-community has meta-mender-tegra-jetpack5 and meta-mender-tegra-jetpack6 on its scarthgap branch; rauc/meta-rauc-community has layers for beaglebone, genericx86-64, nxp, qemu, raspberrypi, rockchip and sunxi but none for Tegra.
Rugix at commit 6d7fc27 (v1.4.0, 2026-11-02) implements boot flows for GRUB, Raspberry Pi tryboot, U-Boot and systemd-boot; no file mentions tegra, jetson, nvbootctrl or l4t as a whole word.
In Linux v6.12, arch/x86, arch/arm64 and arch/riscv Kconfig 'select ARCH_SUPPORTS_RT' (x86 L128, arm64 L105); in v6.11 none of them do, so PREEMPT_RT became buildable from mainline in 6.12.
Debian trixie ships linux-image-rt-amd64, linux-image-rt-arm64 and linux-image-rt-armmp at 6.12.116-1.
Debian kernel 6.12.116-1 base config sets CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y, CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL=y and leaves CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED unset; the rt featureset sets CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT=y.
Linux cgroup-v2 docs: with CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED enabled, the cpu controller can only be enabled when all RT processes are in the root cgroup; the limitation does not apply if it is disabled.

Raspberry Pi's trixie arm64 repo ships PREEMPT_RT kernels only as -rpi-v8-rt builds (6.12.25 to 6.12.75 and 6.18.29 to 6.18.50); no rpi-2712 (Pi 5-optimised) RT package exists; the default linux-image-rpi-2712 is 6.18.60.

Raspberry Pi kernel docs: 'In Linux 6.12 and later, real-time (PREEMPT_RT) support is part of the mainline kernel for 64-bit Arm' and an RT kernel can be built on current branches without a patch; the page states no support for a prebuilt RT kernel.
REP 2000 (Jazzy, May 2024-May 2029): Ubuntu Noble Tier 1 amd64/arm64; RHEL 9 Tier 2; Debian Bookworm Tier 3 (source only); Debian trixie not listed. Tier 3 means the team runs no tests.

ROS 2 Lyrical supported platforms: Ubuntu Resolute (26.04) Tier 1 amd64/arm64, Windows 11 Tier 1, RHEL 10 Tier 2; Ubuntu Noble and Debian Trixie Tier 3 with early EOL (Noble 2029-06-01, Trixie 2028-08-09); Tier 3 needs a source build.
In Lyrical, rmw_zenoh_cpp is a Tier 1 middleware for all architectures, alongside rmw_fastrtps_cpp and rmw_cyclonedds_cpp.
ROS 2 release table: Lyrical released May 22, 2026, EOL May 2031; Kilted EOL December 2026; Jazzy EOL May 2029; Humble EOL May 2027.
Debian trixie has no rclcpp package (packages.debian.org search returned no results), i.e. Debian does not package ROS 2 itself.

Isaac ROS supports Jetson Thor/Orin on JetPack 7.2, x86_64 with Ampere+ GPU on Ubuntu 24.04 (CUDA 13.2+, driver 595+), and DGX Spark on DGX OS 7.2.3; it targets ROS 2 Lyrical; Docker is the recommended option; no other host OS is listed.
rmw_zenoh README: without a Zenoh router 'nodes will not be able to discover each other since multicast discovery is disabled by default'.
Fast DDS docs: shared memory between Docker containers needs --network=host (else they are seen as different hosts and fall back to UDP) and --ipc=host (else they cannot communicate over SHM).
Kubernetes Pod Security Standards Baseline disallows spec.hostNetwork, spec.hostPID and spec.hostIPC and does not allow adding SYS_NICE.
Kubernetes static CPU manager policy (stable since v1.26) gives exclusive CPUs only to containers in Guaranteed pods with integer CPU requests and requires a CPU reservation > 0.

ros2_control: the controller_manager main thread attempts SCHED_FIFO priority 50 regardless of kernel; the docs say a normal kernel is 'not well suited for hardware control' and list Real-time Ubuntu, linux-raspi-realtime and Debian linux-image-rt.
NVIDIA GPU Operator platform-support: 'NVIDIA Jetson, or other embedded products with integrated GPUs, are not supported.'
NVIDIA k8s-device-plugin requires nvidia-container-toolkit >= 1.11.0 to use integrated GPUs on Tegra-based systems.
Clearpath's preferred ROS 2 Jazzy robot install is a 'lightly customized installation image of Ubuntu 24.04' (amd64 only) plus a setup script; the installer wipes the drive.
Boston Dynamics: CORE I/O 4.0.0+ runs JetPack 5.1.2 (L4T R35.4.1); third-party software ships as Docker-based Extensions (introduced in 3.2) with docker-compose, host networking and journald logging.
PX4 docs list ModalAI VOXL 2 as 'Ubuntu 18.04 - Linux Kernel v4.19' on a Qualcomm QRB5165.

AuterionOS and the APX4 flight firmware are 'packaged into a single .auterionos file', updated via Mission Control, Auterion Suite remote updates, or local USB-C web UI upload with verify-then-install.
viam-agent runs as a systemd service on existing Linux, manages viam-server lifecycle, first-boot Wi-Fi/Bluetooth provisioning and OS package updates; it does not install or replace the OS.
PX4 uXRCE-DDS: 'The DDS transport is unauthenticated and reaches uORB directly, so the DDS network must be kept isolated'; PX4 supports only UDP and serial between client and agent.
EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Article 54: 'It shall apply from 14 January 2027' (some articles earlier).

Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III: machinery with self-evolving behaviour must not act beyond its defined task and movement space, and data on safety-related decision-making must be recorded and retained for one year; third-party conformity applies to ML-based safety components (recital 55, Annex I).

Anthropic announced the Model Hardware Standard research preview on 2026-08-27: standardized drivers with read/write primitives, a reference file covering what a device measures, adjusts and 'what safety limits will be enforced', access via MCP, CLI or code; open-source planned with no date; Hugging Face (LeRobot) and Raspberry Pi named as early adopters; no public spec linked.

NVIDIA announced Jetson T3000 (865 FP4 TFLOPS, 32 GB) and T2000 (400 FP4 TFLOPS, 16 GB) on 2026-07-15, 'scheduled to become available in Q1 2027', with T3000 emulation in JetPack 7.2.1 and an IGX T3000 with integrated functional safety.
Linux v6.18 adds drivers/accel/rocket (Rockchip NPU) which v6.17 does not have.
google-coral/edgetpu is archived on GitHub (last push 2021-10-27).
